title: Hobeika 2020 · Collaboration
citation: Hobeika, Taffou, and Viaud-Delmon (2020). Social impact on audiotactile integration near the body. Acoustical Science and Technology, 41(1), 345–348.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.relationship: The parallel Royal Society Open Science report has the same three assessments, analyzed counts and multiple statistics. Participant-level overlap is unverified.
published_method.audio: Three-second binaural bubbling water at −60° or +60°, approaching from 135 to 20 cm in an IRCAM Spat room simulation with LISTEN HRTFs.
published_method.sound_gaps: Original waveform, renderer patch and calibration are unavailable.
published_method.tactile: 20 ms, 250 Hz sinusoid delivered by a 28 mm miniature loudspeaker to palmar left index.
published_method.baselines: Periods nominally −650 and +3650 ms relative to sound onset, using actual silent windows around sound in the thesis procedure.
published_method.posture: Seated in a fixed side position, hands covered, partner at 100 cm in dyad compared with isolated condition.
published_method.response: Speeded right-finger response to touch, withhold on audio-only. Analyze effects by sound side and social context.
published_method.dyad_instruction: Dyad instruction frames both partners as pursuing a combined performance goal.

stimulus_type.value: Bubbling-water sound plus palmar index vibration

implementation_gaps: Requires shared-clock coordination for two participants, routed and calibrated physical tactile and response paths, and the original audio rendering assets.
The exact per-block trial manifest, ITI draw distribution and response cutoff are unavailable. Silent-window tactile probes retain the sound sequence.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
